correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the d=m+n-1 Lipschitz dual quotient norm L=max_{i,j}|x_i-y_j|, since all same-part distances equal 2 and are implied by cross-edge bounds. A point of its unit polytope is a vertex exactly when the tight-edge subgraph is connected; this forces either constant part classes differing by 1 or one class zero and the other ±1. For Q0=h²+mean u²+mean v² every listed vertex has Q0=1, so Q0<=L² by convexity; the cross-edge functional has squared Q0 dual norm d, giving L²<=dQ0, and an explicit witness attains both boundaries. Symmetrization of arbitrary positive quadratic forms under S_m×S_n reduces them without loss to alpha sum u_i²+beta sum v_j²+gamma h². Constant and balanced-sign vertices give gamma<=1 and the parity delta bounds. The crossing-edge dual norm G >= d follows from reciprocal-gamma and c_s inequalities (c_m+c_n<=1/2), and quadratic duality implies distortion >=sqrt(d). Independent exact Fraction tests for (m,n)=(3,3),(3,4),(4,5),(6,7) checked all sign vertices, the witness and the gamma certificates. These bounded checks are auxiliary.
residual_risks: Unit-edge graph shortest-path metric K_{m,n}, m,n>=3, real scalars only; no arbitrary weighted bipartite graph or complex analogue.
Verification script covers only m,n<=8 and some rational invariant quadratic coefficients; the proof establishes all pairs.

originality.rationale: Alexander–Fradelizi–García-Lirola–Zvavitch full preprint covers the exact graph geometry, characterizes K_{2,n} spiderwebs and Hanner free-space balls but does not optimize Hilbert Banach–Mazur distance for K_{m,n}, m,n>=3. Dilworth–Kutzarova–Ostrovskii treat ell_1 comparisons and recursive graph families. Indexed exact graph BM formulas for even cycles, weighted cycles and equilateral spaces do not imply the whole two-parameter complete-bipartite result; neither does bipartite numerical index 1.
residual_risks: Unindexed transportation-cost polytope ellipsoid theorem under graphical root-polytope or matrix-norm terminology may cover this family.
Real, unit-edge and m,n>=3 assumptions are essential; Hanner status alone proves neither inequality.
